nodes.label: Naming Convention Rule
nodes.rationale: Entity properties mirror lowercase Postgres column names because the entities are scaffolded and the DB is the source of truth, so camelCase/PascalCase must not be introduced there even though it is used everywhere else (e.g. request.teamName).

nodes.label: Aspire AppHost
nodes.rationale: AppHost references the other projects only as orchestration resources, so their NuGet packages do not flow into it transitively; package fixes must be pinned in AppHost directly when needed.

nodes.label: Hangfire Background Jobs
nodes.rationale: Schedule polling runs at 1s, which bounds draft-timer precision.

nodes.label: BoxScoreFactory / BoxScoreBuilder
nodes.rationale: BoxScoreStatsBuilder fabricates randomized dummy player game stats as a stand-in until the balldontlie player-stats subscription is paid for. Whether real fantasy scoring should instead read the per-league Statsvalue table, rather than the hardcoded BoxScoreEvaluation multipliers, is an explicit undecided TODO, so both paths are deliberately left in place.

nodes.label: DraftTimerHostedService
nodes.rationale: Polls the draft:timers Redis sorted set every second for pick deadlines; this intentionally replaces per-pick Hangfire jobs.

nodes.label: NBA.Tests
nodes.rationale: Pure unit tests (mapping, adapter, JWT, Argon2 hashing) that need no Docker/Postgres/Redis, so dotnet test runs standalone without the Aspire stack.

nodes.label: Authenticate Everything Rule
nodes.rationale: Only /health, /alive, /redis-check, login/signup, GET /v1/players and GET /v1/games are anonymous because the web dashboard shows the player pool and NBA schedule to signed-out visitors and neither response is user-specific.

nodes.label: DTOs at the API Boundary
nodes.rationale: EF entities are never returned directly from endpoints; mapping through NBA.Api/Mappings keeps the persistence model separate from the API contract. Request DTOs use camelCase, response DTOs mirror the entity casing they map from.

nodes.label: NBAException Error Handling Rule
nodes.rationale: Standardizing on NBAException + ErrorCodes (adding a new ErrorCode when none fits) lets GlobalExceptionHandler translate every domain failure into a consistent response shape instead of ad-hoc exceptions.

nodes.label: Redis Access Layer Facade Rule
nodes.rationale: NbaFantasyRedis is a Facade injecting each *Operations dependency as Lazy<T> so Redis logic stays centralized; keys are always built from the RedisKeys static key builders, never inlined, to prevent key-format drift.

nodes.label: external-api-shield Resilience Pipeline Rule
nodes.rationale: Any new outbound HTTP call must go through the named external-api-shield pipeline (retry + concurrency limiter) to protect the system against unreliable external APIs such as balldontlie.

nodes.label: Schema Changes Live in infrastructure/
nodes.rationale: There are no EF migrations; the SQL scripts under infrastructure/db/create and db/seed are the source of truth, so any table/column change must be made there and mirrored in the matching NBA.Data/Entities class.

nodes.label: Service vs Manager Split
nodes.rationale: Logic is split by backing store: *Service classes manipulate data in PostgreSQL, *Manager classes work against Redis, keeping persistence concerns separated by store.

nodes.label: SignalR Auth via Query String
nodes.rationale: Browsers can't set the Authorization header on a WebSocket, so the JWT is read from the ?access_token= query string for /draftHub and /chatHub (see OnMessageReceived in Program.cs).
